title: Causal Inference for Recommendation: Foundations, Methods and Applications

bias_targets.methodology: Reviewed approaches use reweighting methods like Inverse Propensity Scoring (IPS) to handle missing-not-at-random (MNAR) explicit feedback.
Reviewed approaches apply causal adjustment (such as back-door adjustment) and Inverse Propensity Scoring (IPS) to adjust for unobserved implicit feedback and uneven item exposure.
Reviewed approaches utilize causal graphs and causal embeddings to disentangle users' true personal interests from group conformity behaviors.
Reviewed approaches apply Inverse Propensity Scoring (IPS) and reweighting to correct for users' tendency to interact with higher-ranked items regardless of relevance.
Reviewed approaches employ causal adjustments (front-door/back-door), Inverse Propensity Scoring (IPS), and counterfactual reasoning to mitigate the over-recommendation of widely popular items.

Reviewed approaches measure and mitigate unfairness using counterfactual data augmentation, causal-based fairness metrics (like Average Treatment effect on the Treated), and structural causal models to identify and remove discrimination pathways.
Reviewed approaches use unbiased data injections and random recommendation policies (experimental data) to break the cycle of amplified bias and filter bubbles.
